Pricing
Plans & Upgrades

Choose the plan that matches your workflow intensity and AI usage needs.

How to use it
• Compare Free and Pro features.
• Select monthly or yearly billing.
• Start checkout and complete activation with your email.
Pro tips
• Use yearly billing if you plan to trade consistently.
• Match plan tier to your expected AI and backtest usage.
Open Tool →
Auth
Sign In & Activation

Authenticate with your checkout email to activate session and tool access.

How to use it
• Enter the same email used during checkout.
• Wait for activation confirmation and redirect.
• If needed, restart checkout from pricing when no subscription is found.
Pro tips
• Use one primary billing email for all devices.
• Check spam folder if verification-related messages are delayed.
Open Tool →
Account
Account Settings

Manage subscription, view plan features, and access referral tools.

How to use it
• Review your current tier and account email.
• Open billing portal for subscription changes.
• Copy/share referral links and track referral stats.
Pro tips
• Reconfirm plan access after upgrades or cancellations.
• Use referral links directly from account for clean tracking.
Open Tool →
Tools Hub
Tools Workspace

Use the tools hub to choose your workflow: discover, validate, test, and review.

How to use it
• Choose your current task: scanning, planning, testing, or review.
• Open the matching tool and confirm market/risk context first.
• Move outcomes into alerts, portfolio, and journal for continuity.
Pro tips
• Run a consistent daily sequence to avoid context switching.
• Favor depth over tool-hopping when conditions are noisy.
Open Tool →
Private
Private Research Dashboard

Private internal dashboard for reviewing presence, context, and workflow state.

How to use it
• Check presence mode and context state first.
• Review top-attention symbols and confidence context.
• Compare suggested next checks with risk posture before escalating a scenario.
Pro tips
• Use feedback buttons after each review to improve adaptation.
• Treat controlMatrix output as internal research state, not public advice.
Open Tool →
Scanner
Market Scanner

Scan symbols, evaluate setup quality, and promote high-confidence candidates into plans.

How to use it
• Run a scan with your selected asset class and timeframe.
• Inspect confidence, direction, and confluence evidence.
• Promote pass-grade candidates and review generated plan details.
Pro tips
• Use tighter watchlists when volatility is high.
• Prioritize symbols with stable directional agreement across signals.
Open Tool →
Options
Options Confluence

Combine options flow, IV context, and structure to produce higher-quality setups.

How to use it
• Load symbol and timeframe, then run confluence analysis.
• Check confluence tier, key levels, and strategy classification.
• Promote pass outcomes into workflow plans and alerts.
Pro tips
• Guided mode is faster for analysis; Advanced mode is better for diagnostics.
• Avoid forcing setups when volatility regime and flow disagree.
Open Tool →
Alerts
Alerts Center

Create automated conditions and monitor triggered events across your watch universe.

How to use it
• Define symbol, condition, and threshold.
• Enable recurring checks and notification preferences.
• Review triggered alerts and send relevant ones to journal/workflow.
Pro tips
• Use fewer, higher-conviction alerts to reduce noise.
• Tie alerts to planned entry zones instead of arbitrary prices.
Open Tool →
Portfolio
Portfolio Tracking

Track exposure, concentration, and performance to maintain risk discipline.

How to use it
• Review open positions and aggregate exposure.
• Check concentration and drawdown before adding risk.
• Use performance history to evaluate consistency over time.
Pro tips
• High concentration should reduce new position sizing.
• Use drawdown state as a hard guardrail for pace.
Open Tool →
Journal
Trade Journal

Capture execution decisions and outcomes to improve repeatability and edge quality.

How to use it
• Log entries with setup, side, and rationale.
• Record exits and classify outcome quality.
• Review stats and recurring behavior patterns weekly.
Pro tips
• Write why you entered before the trade, not after.
• Track mistakes with consistent tags for cleaner analytics.
Open Tool →
Backtest
Strategy Backtester

Validate strategy assumptions on historical data before risking live capital.

How to use it
• Select symbol, strategy, timeframe, and period.
• Run test and inspect win rate, profit factor, and drawdown.
• Promote robust configurations into plan templates.
Pro tips
• Prioritize stability metrics over single-period returns.
• Retest after any strategy parameter change.
Open Tool →
MSP AI
MSP AI

Use the floating AI research panel beside live Scanner context.

How to use it
• Ask a focused market or scenario question.
• Compare the response against scanner evidence and data quality.
• Convert useful research context into alerts, plans, or journal notes.
Pro tips
• Use specific symbols and timeframes for higher-quality output.
• Treat AI output as research support, not personal advice.
Open Tool →
Markets
Markets Overview

Monitor broad market conditions before drilling into symbol-level execution.

How to use it
• Start with market trend and breadth context.
• Identify sectors or themes with strongest relative momentum.
• Move qualified opportunities into scanner or watchlists.
Pro tips
• Use this as your daily top-down checkpoint.
• Avoid trading against dominant market regime.
Open Tool →
Movers
Market Movers

Track strongest gainers and losers for momentum and mean-reversion opportunities.

How to use it
• Review top movers and liquidity profile.
• Filter for symbols matching your strategy profile.
• Send qualified symbols to scanner or alerts.
Pro tips
• Confirm follow-through with volume, not price alone.
• Avoid thin names during high-spread sessions.
Open Tool →
Watchlists
Watchlists

Organize symbols by strategy so scans and alerts stay focused.

How to use it
• Create strategy-specific watchlists.
• Add high-conviction symbols with clean thesis notes.
• Feed watchlists into scanner and alert workflows.
Pro tips
• Smaller focused lists outperform giant mixed lists.
• Archive stale symbols weekly.
Open Tool →
News
News Feed

Use macro and company catalysts to avoid blind technical setups.

How to use it
• Scan headlines by symbol/theme.
• Mark actionable catalysts.
• Adjust risk and timing around event windows.
Pro tips
• Price reaction matters more than headline tone.
• Avoid new entries right before binary events.
Open Tool →
Macro
Macro Dashboard

Track macro drivers that shift risk appetite and trend persistence.

How to use it
• Review key macro indicators.
• Map macro regime to current strategy bias.
• Adjust position sizing by regime risk.
Pro tips
• Treat macro as context, not single-signal triggers.
• Reduce aggression in mixed macro regimes.
Open Tool →
Leaders
Gainers & Losers

Identify leadership and weakness quickly for intraday prioritization.

How to use it
• Open top gainers/losers tables.
• Validate with liquidity and structure.
• Queue candidates into scanner.
Pro tips
• Leadership rotation can invalidate old watchlist priorities.
• Beware one-candle spikes with no structure.
Open Tool →
Heatmap
Heatmap

Visualize strength clusters across sectors and assets.

How to use it
• Read hot/cold clusters.
• Drill into strongest sectors.
• Cross-check with scanner confidence.
Pro tips
• Use heatmaps for direction, scanner for execution.
• Look for broad participation, not isolated spikes.
Open Tool →
Equity
Equity Explorer

Research equities with structured market, technical, and context data.

How to use it
• Search symbol fundamentals/context.
• Validate trend and volatility conditions.
• Promote symbols to plans/alerts as needed.
Pro tips
• Check earnings proximity before planning entries.
• Use explorer for thesis, scanner for timing.
Open Tool →
Company
Company Overview

Get quick business-level context before committing trade risk.

How to use it
• Load company profile and key metrics.
• Review business and valuation context.
• Integrate with technical setup quality.
Pro tips
• Avoid mismatch between thesis horizon and trade timeframe.
• Use overview to spot narrative risk.
Open Tool →
Charts
Intraday Charts

Use structured chart views to refine levels and invalidation.

How to use it
• Select symbol and timeframe.
• Apply key indicators and levels.
• Define reference/invalidation/key level zones.
Pro tips
• One clean setup beats many noisy micro-signals.
• Mark invalidation before acting.
Open Tool →
Earnings
Earnings Intelligence

Evaluate earnings-driven volatility and event risk inside Market Intelligence.

How to use it
• Review upcoming earnings names.
• Assess implied volatility context.
• Adjust scenario timing around report windows.
Pro tips
• Binary event risk warrants conservative assumptions.
• Avoid relying on unclear evidence through reports.
Open Tool →
Calendar
Earnings Calendar

Track report schedules to avoid accidental event exposure.

How to use it
• Filter by date and relevance.
• Tag symbols with pending events.
• Route flagged names into watchlists/alerts.
Pro tips
• Use pre/post-market timing details.
• Pair with scanner to reprioritize daily focus.
Open Tool →
Macro Events
Economic Calendar

Plan trading around high-impact macro releases.

How to use it
• Check high-impact events first.
• Align intraday risk windows.
• Lower exposure into uncertain prints.
Pro tips
• Volatility often starts before release time.
• Prioritize survival over prediction on event days.
Open Tool →
Crypto
Crypto Markets

Monitor crypto market structure, trend shifts, and opportunity flow.

How to use it
• Review dominant trend and breadth.
• Identify relative strength leaders.
• Promote actionable setups to scanner/alerts.
Pro tips
• Respect funding and liquidation risk during spikes.
• Use smaller size in unstable regime transitions.
Open Tool →
Crypto Derivatives
Crypto Derivatives

Central view for crypto momentum, derivatives sentiment, and risk context.

How to use it
• Check dominance/funding/open-interest context.
• Confirm directional consensus.
• Review only when context and setup align.
Pro tips
• Derivatives extremes often precede reversals.
• Treat dashboard as context layer, not direct trigger.
Open Tool →
Crypto Explorer
Crypto Explorer

Deep dive into individual crypto assets for analysis.

How to use it
• Select asset and review structure.
• Inspect volatility and participation.
• Map reference levels and risk constraints.
Pro tips
• Use explorer for selection, scanner for timing context.
• Avoid forcing low-liquidity assets.
Open Tool →
Crypto Heatmap
Crypto Heatmap

Visualize sector-level momentum and risk rotation in crypto.

How to use it
• Read strongest/weakest clusters.
• Prioritize liquid leaders.
• Cross-check with confluence signals before acting.
Pro tips
• Look for broad alignment in top assets.
• Ignore isolated outliers without confirmation.
Open Tool →
Confluence
Confluence Scanner

Combine multiple factors into one score to rank setup quality.

How to use it
• Run confluence scan for your universe.
• Inspect score components and regime fit.
• Promote top setups into plan workflow.
Pro tips
• Guided mode is ideal for speed.
• Use advanced diagnostics when confidence is borderline.
Open Tool →
Deep Analysis
Golden Egg Deep Analysis

Generate structured multi-factor analysis for high-conviction decisions.

How to use it
• Run deep analysis on selected symbol.
• Review confidence and risk factors.
• Convert strong outputs into actionable plans.
Pro tips
• Use this for fewer but higher-quality decisions.
• Document assumptions in journal before execution.
Open Tool →
AI Tools
AI Tools

Use the current workflow and MSP AI instead of the retired AI tools collection.

How to use it
• Start from the workflow map.
• Open the live research tool that matches the question.
• Use MSP AI for context, then validate against evidence.
Pro tips
• Specific prompts produce better output.
• Always validate outputs against source data.
Open Tool →
Commodities
Commodities

Track commodity markets with structure, trend, and macro context.

How to use it
• Review commodity trend state.
• Check macro drivers and volatility.
• Promote clean setups into scanner/alerts.
Pro tips
• Commodities react strongly to macro surprises.
• Use tighter risk in event-heavy sessions.
Open Tool →

METHODOLOGY & GLOSSARY

How our scores work

MarketScanner Pros is an educational market-analysis platform. Every score it shows is a composite summary of evidence — not a statistical probability, not a forecast, and never a personalised instruction to buy, sell, or hold. This page explains exactly what each score, badge, and state means so you can judge the evidence for yourself.

Scores are composite strength, not probability

A number like Composite Strength 78 / 100 (also shown as MSP Score or Confluence in places) is a weighted summary of how much of the current evidence points one way. It is a heuristic — the weights are rules chosen for transparency, not calibrated against historical outcomes. A 78 does not mean a 78% chance of anything. Where a tooltip says “reflects how many indicators agree, not a probability,” that is the literal truth of the number.

Independent factor groups

Many indicators measure the same thing. EMA position, MACD, ADX, and Aroon are all expressions of trend. If four of them agree, that is one piece of trend evidence — not four. To avoid overstating agreement, we collapse correlated indicators into a small set of independent factor groups and count agreement across the groups:

Trend — EMA structure, MACD, ADX/DI, Aroon
Momentum — RSI, Stochastic, CCI
Participation / Volume — OBV, MFI, VWAP, relative volume
Volatility — BBWP, ATR, DVE phase
Relative strength — vs a benchmark (SPY for equities, BTC for crypto)
Market structure — levels, breakout proximity, EMA stack
Positioning — funding, open interest, liquidations (crypto)
Regime — trend / range / risk-on / risk-off context
Macro / cross-asset — DXY, rates, VIX regime
Catalyst — earnings and scheduled events
Evidence quality

Evidence quality grades the inputs behind a conclusion — how many independent factors are available, how fresh the data is, and whether factors conflict. It caps the composite: poor or stale evidence cannot produce a high headline number.

HIGH
Broad coverage, current data, no major conflicts.
MEDIUM
Adequate coverage; some data delayed or a factor missing.
LOW
Sparse coverage, stale data, or conflicting factors.
INSUFFICIENT
Too few independent factors, or data missing/simulated — treat as exploratory only.
Setup stage

A description of observable behaviour — where a move appears to be in its lifecycle. It is context for research, not a trade instruction.

Dormant
Quiet; nothing developing.
Building
Participation rising while price is still contained — the early signal.
Confirming
Independent factors agree and price is beginning to validate the move.
Expanding
Participation and price expanding together with rising volatility.
Extended
A significant move has already occurred; the early window has passed.
Fading
Participation or momentum deteriorating after a move.
Extension state

How far a move has already run, from distance-from-average, range, and volatility percentile. Early / Normal / Elevated / Extreme. An Extreme reading means the obvious part of the move may already be behind it — context, not a signal.

Data freshness & provenance

Every data source carries a freshness badge: Live (current within the expected provider cadence), Delayed, Stale, or Missing. Panel-level badges reflect the weakest underlying row — a panel will not show “Live” over degraded or cached data. Delayed data is never presented as real-time.

Derived vs observed data

Some readings are estimated, not directly observed, and are labelled as such. Where a reading comes from a single venue it says so: for example, “Long/Short (OKX accounts)” is OKX’s reported count of accounts net long versus net short, not position size and not the whole market. We label derived, delayed, estimated, and simulated data so you can weight it accordingly.

Market regime

Regime is the broad environment — trending, range, risk-on, risk-off, expansion, compression. The same indicator can mean different things in different regimes, so regime is shown as persistent context. When evidence is thin, the platform is comfortable saying Mixed / Conflicting or Unknown rather than forcing a call.

We do not present composite scores as statistical probabilities.
We do not issue buy / sell / hold instructions or personalised financial advice.
We do not connect to brokers or route orders — portfolio and backtest features are simulation only.
We do not publish fake testimonials, invented usage statistics, or guaranteed returns.
We do not present delayed, estimated, or simulated data as live, observed data.
